title: Three Springs and One Short Trowel
subtitle: 植物农业 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 植物农业（人与自然·自然生态·植物与农业）
meta: 主题语境：植物农业（人与自然·自然生态·植物与农业）　|　核心词汇：row　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 row 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1986 the gardener ① planted the row that no apprentice in the garden would have noted, and he said the planting was the whole of the spring. The ② row, meaning the line itself and not the trowel, ran three springs and stayed unnoted in the book; a row, he said, is the only thing in a garden that is judged by how long it is left unnoted.

Every ③ row in that garden had the same short trowel beside it, and the ④ row at the far bed, meaning the cutting they kept for the children to plant and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A row, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to note; the gardener said the noting is the part that fills three springs.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the row was the whole of the matter, meaning the order and not the line. The ⑥ row, meaning the order and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody notes; row, he said, is either something you plant or the only word that means both a line and an order. He said the order is the part they remember.

By 1991 the ⑦ row had become a line in a notebook, and the notebook had become an argument about the short trowel. The ⑧ row of the whole thing, the gardener wrote in April, was one garden and three springs of noting; row, he said, is either the cutting at the far bed or the reason you learned to note. He said the noting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ row I remember is the line noted in the notebook, which closed in 1993 and is still noted as the quietest in the garden. A ⑩ row, my mother said in 1995, is the only line that improves by being noted; every row, she said, is an order that has agreed to look like a line. She said the order was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 一排；一行（指园子里每一排旁边的那一排）
B. n. 一排；一行（指那排一排本身，与小小的花铲相对）
C. 固定搭配：plant the row 种成这一排一排
D. n. 一排；一行（指留给孩子们插的那一枝）
E. n. 一排之事（抽象总称，指一处园子的一排之事）
F. n. 一排；一行（指园艺笔记里写到、被记下的那一排）
G. n. 一排、次序（指一件事里人人都种却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 次序（抽象总称，指人人都种却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: planted the row that no apprentice in the garden would have noted
The row, meaning the line itself and not the trowel
the row at the far bed

answers.why: plant the row 意为“种成这一排一排”，1986 年那位园丁把园子里没有一位学徒肯记下的一排一排做了一遍。
row 意为“一排；一行”，指那排一排本身而不是小小的花铲，它经过了三个春天而在簿子上没有被记下。
row 意为“一排；一行”，指园子里每一排旁边的那一排，每一排旁边都有同一把小小的花铲。
row 意为“一排；一行”，指最远那畦苗床的留给孩子们插的那一枝，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
row 意为“一排、次序”，指一件事里人人都种却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这排次序就是那件事的全部。
row 意为“次序”，指人人都种却无人提起的那样东西而不是那排一排，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
row 意为“一排；一行”，指园艺笔记里写到、被记下的那一排，到 1991 年这一排成了园艺笔记里的一行。
row 意为“一排之事”，园丁四月写道，整件事的一排之事是一处园子和三个春天的记下。
row 意为“一排；一行”，我记得的是园艺笔记里记下过的那一排，1993 年栽完了，至今仍被说成园子里最安静的一排。
row 为抽象总称，母亲 1995 年说，一排是唯一会因为被好好记下而变得更好的一排。
